items.title: Quick hits: Canada's emotional match-winner and South Korea's team blasted
items.description: Canada's heroes tread new ground, South Korea's extreme reaction to going out and scenes in Algeria's home away from home. Here's the five quick hits from the World Cup.

items.title: Live: Taylor brushes off low polling and says rebuilding trust takes time
items.description: Opposition Leader Angus Taylor says it will take time for the Coalition to win back the trust of voters. Follow live.

items.title: Baby, young boys pulled alive from Venezuela earthquake rubble
items.description: The three children are among at least 33 people rescued during a weekend multinational operation that continued searching for survivors, while thousands remained unaccounted-for.

items.title: Royal commission spotlight falls on 'unregulated cesspool of disinformation'
items.description: The "cesspool" of anti-Jewish material on social media is set to be examined when the antisemitism royal commission resumes this week.

items.title: Real estate has been an easy target for criminals laundering money, until now
items.description: Anti-money laundering laws mean that for the first time, real estate agents, lawyers, accountants and others must report suspicious transactions.

items.title: 'It's shocking': ASIC says too many Australians' retirement savings are being wiped out
items.description: The corporate watchdog is concerned that super trustees that manage Australians' retirement savings have a lack of safeguards in place.

items.title: Dozens of former Australian Rules footballers diagnosed with CTE
items.description: Australian Rules footballers who never played in the game's premier league are being diagnosed with CTE, revealing that the brain trauma crisis is striking all levels of the game.

items.title: Last week was a turning point inside the Liberal party
items.description: While Angus Taylor grapples with the Coalition's dilemma of how to keep the centre while diverting voters away from Pauline Hanson's party, Andrew Hastie has been talking tough on One Nation.

items.title: Two things this week gave clues about the global future
items.description: Two things happened last week that give us a much clearer picture of what the world is going to be like from now on.

items.title: The Gulf will 'not go back to where it was' after the Iran war
items.description: Before a flare-up in fighting over the weekend, the interim deal between the United States and Iran was giving the region something it badly needs, analysts say.

items.title: President Trump Announces U.S. Military Airstrike in Venezuela
items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.title: Trump Meets Netanyahu at Mar-a-Lago for Gaza Ceasefire Phase Two Talks
items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.title: Feds Launch Massive Taxpayer Fraud Probe in Minnesota After Viral Video
items.description: Federal agencies including DHS, FBI, and ICE investigate $110 million in suspected fraud at Minnesota child care centers following a viral YouTube video[3].

items.title: Americans Express Widespread Opposition to AI Data Centers
items.description: Public backlash against AI infrastructure data centers grows, with protests and demands for bans influencing Democratic Party strategies for future elections[3].

items.title: Elon Musk's Humanoid Robot Vision: China Poised to Lead Production
items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].

items.title: Trump-Putin Call Amid Ukraine-Russia Tensions Over Peace Plan
items.description: President Trump spoke with Putin amid ongoing Ukraine conflict, with Russia reevaluating peace plan tenets after Ukrainian denials[1].

items.title: Democratic Gubernatorial Candidates in Wisconsin Focus on Inflation and Trump
items.description: Seven Democrats vying for Wisconsin governor blame economic issues on Trump and emphasize affordability ahead of 2026 primary[3].
